subject: Clarifying service-provider language & data flow for US privacy addendum
messages:

Subject: Question on 'service provider' language and data flows for US addendum

Hi Olga —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our privacy team has a couple quick follow-ups before procurement can sign the US state privacy addendum:

1) We want to confirm whether Redwood’s standard DPA/addendum treats you as a "service provider" under CCPA/CPRA terms or as a "processor" in technical terms. Our counsel is concerned about any residual language that could be interpreted as a "sale" or as allowing secondary use beyond providing the service.

2) Can you share your current subprocessors list and indicate whether any subprocessors will process household or device identifiers that could be considered personal data under state laws?

3) Cross-border: we need to confirm whether telemetry/analytics or support logs might be transferred outside the US and if so what controls (e.g., encryption, KMS) apply.

Procurement would like to get the addendum signed this month if possible. Would appreciate a short note addressing these points and any doc links.

Best,
Elena
Privacy Manager, ACME Health

Subject: Re: Question on 'service provider' language and data flows for US addendum

Hi all —

Quick legal note on the ACME questions:

1) Service provider vs processor: for US state addenda (CCPA/CPRA and similar state laws) we explicitly accept the "service provider" designation for covered personal information. Our standard clause: "Provider acts as a Service Provider (not a Controller) and will Process Customer Personal Information only to provide the Services as directed in the Agreement; Provider will not Sell Personal Information, nor use it for its own purposes." We can surface that sentence in the addendum and add a cross-reference to the DPA.

2) Subprocessors: we maintain an up-to-date list (attached). Our standard approach is: (a) notify customers of material changes; (b) allow reasonable objection for defined categories in some enterprise agreements; (c) require subprocessors to be bound by our DPA obligations. For ACME: we can include a 30-day prior notice and a carve-out that requires ACME to notify procurement if a subprocessor is handling household/device identifiers so we can assess.

3) Cross-border transfers & telemetry: telemetry and aggregated, non-identifiable metrics are generally used for service health and performance; any logs containing personal data are stored in US regions by default but may be replicated to our EU/ASIA DR regions for resilience. Controls: data at rest is encrypted; customer-specific keys via KMS can be supported (bring-your-own-key options) for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted customers we offer KMS integration for key rotation and HSM-backed key storage on request (may be part of an enterprise addendum).

Suggested redline snippet for the addendum (short):
"Provider affirms it is a Service Provider under applicable US privacy laws and will not Sell Personal Information. Provider will process Personal Information only on Customer's documented instructions in the Agreement. Provider may engage Subprocessors; Provider will maintain a subprocessors list and provide 30 days' notice of material changes. Customer may object to a new Subprocessor with reasonable cause; Provider will pause the new engagement while parties seek a resolution. Cross-border transfers of Personal Information will be secured via encryption at rest and in transit; upon Customer request Provider will support customer-managed keys where operationally available."
I can prepare a concise addendum redline for ACME to sign and include the subprocessor CSV. If ACME needs additional contractual guarantees (e.g., specific retention windows, audit rights), we should document those as specific addendum clauses.

-Neha
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@acmehealth.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on 'service provider' language and data flows for US addendum

Elena —

Attaching the artifacts you asked for: redwood_dpa_v3.pdf (current DPA), subprocessors_list_2026-04.csv (current list), and a short security factsheet. Summary answers:

- Subprocessors: none of the listed subprocessors are used to "sell" data; most are cloud infra, monitoring, and analytics partners. I highlighted in the CSV the partners that handle logs/metrics.
- Data retention & deletion: default retention for logs that may include identifiers is 90 days; we can adjust by contractual exception (e.g., 30/90/365) for enterprise customers. Deletion is implemented via expunge APIs and verified via audit logs.
- KMS: for hosted customers we offer customer-managed keys on request; Dedicated/Private deployments support B/Y/O keys and HSM integrations.

Link to a simple dataflow diagram: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c_dataflow_diagram

If ACME wants, we can: (a) add a 30-day notification clause for subprocessors; (b) include a retention paragraph specifying 90 days by default and an option to shorten; and (c) include the no-sale language Neha suggested.

Marissa Cole
Privacy & Trust, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dpa_v3.pdf (DPA, 28 pages), subprocessors_list_2026-04.csv (3 KB), redwood_security_factsheet.pdf (2 pages)
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@acmehealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>, Bass & Reed Counsel <privacy@bassreed.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on 'service provider' language and data flows for US addendum

Thanks — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from our side before we can sign:

- Procurement would like the default retention to be 90 days but wants the addendum to explicitly state that ACME can request a 30-day retention window for identifiers and have Redwood implement it within 30 days of the request.
- Counsel wants the 30-day notice for new subprocessors and an explicit objection mechanism; if Redwood pauses onboarding while we review, that is acceptable.
- For telemetry: we need confirmation that PII-containing logs will not be replicated outside the US without prior notice and written consent. If replication for DR is required, we need assurance that customer-managed KMS will be used (or that data will be anonymized).

If you can send a DocuSign-ready addendum with those three points (retention option, subprocessor notice/objection, and replication/KMS assurances), procurement can execute quickly.

-Elena
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@acmehealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Bass & Reed Counsel <privacy@bassreed.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on 'service provider' language and data flows for US addendum

Elena / Procurement —

Thanks for the clear asks. I’ve attached a short redline that incorporates: (1) default 90-day retention with a contractual option to require 30-day retention for identifiers (Provider to implement within 30 days of written request), (2) 30-day subprocessor notice with an objection process and temporary pause for onboarding while parties resolve objections, and (3) express language that PII-containing logs will not be replicated outside the US without written consent; DR replication is permitted only with customer-managed keys or anonymization.

DocuSign link to the addendum and execution package: https://www.docusign.com/templates/ACME-addendum-2026

Next steps:
- ACME signs via DocuSign (target: 48–72 hours)
- Redwood legal will confirm the KMS onboarding checklist once signed and target implementation within two business weeks for hosted customers (quicker for Dedicated).
- I’ll share a formal statement for procurement that references the subprocessors CSV and security factsheet.

If that timeline works, I’ll move the package to DocuSign now.

Olga
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
